quote: Lest you think this a trivial ability, remember how rare it is in the animal kingdom.
content: The essay does not deny mice uncertainty monitoring. Declining a hard trial requires registering that this trial feels difficult. It does not require representing that one has a visual system whose construction produces systematic illusions, which is the "mental bucket" for the lens that the essay describes. The note's own conclusion is the essay's: "What humans can do that rats cannot is distrust the picture." The essay never said that knowing about the Müller-Lyer illusion makes the lines look equal. It said "You don't always have to believe your own eyes," which is distrusting the picture, and it credits that ability to humans alone.

quote: then you can apply a reflective correction
content: The corrections the debiasing literature endorses are reflective corrections. Checklists, considering the opposite and reformatting a problem are procedures that someone designed after understanding a bias, which is the second-order move the essay describes. Individual training also works better than the note reports. A single session of interactive training reduced anchoring, the bias blind spot, confirmation bias and other errors, and the effects lasted at least two months (Morewedge et al. 2015). The training also carried over to an unannounced field problem weeks later (Sellier, Scopelliti & Morewedge 2019). The essay claimed "not perfect, but far more powerful," and that is what was measured.

quote: Pondering this business of “performing replicable experiments to falsify theories,” we can see why it works.
content: The sentence puts "performing replicable experiments to falsify theories" in quotation marks and then says something different about it: "The whole idea of Science is, simply, reflective reasoning about a more reliable process for making the contents of your mind mirror the contents of the world." That is not falsificationism. It is the claim that science can be explained as a process that tracks truth, and Lakatos's research programmes, Kuhn's paradigms and the Bayesian reconstructions of both are all attempts to do exactly that. The later essays that "reject" Traditional Rationality replace it with a process that is better understood, which is the lens seeing its own flaws a second time. A method understood well enough to be improved on supports the essay's thesis; it is not a counterexample to it.
